```{=html}
<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Appendix B <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Proofs &amp; Comments</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">B.10</span> Tensoriality of the torsion (§<a class="dg-xref" href="../covariant-derivative/torsion-curvature.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Torsion_Curvature">6.4</a>)</h1></header>
<p>In this appendix, we prove that the torsion of a connection <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span>, <span class="math display">\[
    \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \coloneqq df\left\lceil \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \right\rfloor,
    \qquad
    \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \coloneqq \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X} - [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}] \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M},
\]</span> is <span class="math inline">\(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>-linear in its first and second entries, i.e. that for all <span class="math inline">\(g \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(df, dh \in \Gamma T^*\mathcal{M}\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{Z} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M}\)</span>, <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
    \mathtt{T}(g \, df + dh, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y})          &amp;= g \, \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) + \mathtt{T}(dh, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}), \\
    \mathtt{T}(df, g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}) &amp;= g \, \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) + \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}),
\end{align*}</span> where, as in Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../covariant-derivative/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Covariant_Derivative">6</a>, sums and s-multiplications of fields are written in compact notation. We will only need the following facts, all established in the main text:</p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li class="dg-labelled"><span class="dg-item-label">(a)</span> <p>The action of a covector field is <span class="math inline">\(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>-linear in the vector field, <span class="math inline">\(df\left\lceil g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z} \right\rfloor = g \, df\left\lceil \mathcal{X} \right\rfloor + df\left\lceil \mathcal{Z} \right\rfloor\)</span>, which holds point-wise by linearity of <span class="math inline">\((df)_p\)</span>, since <span class="math inline">\((g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z})(p) = g(p) \, \mathcal{X}(p) + \mathcal{Z}(p)\)</span>.</p></li>
<li class="dg-labelled"><span class="dg-item-label">(b)</span> <p>The module operations of <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma T\mathcal{M}\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma T^*\mathcal{M}\)</span> act point-wise on the actions: <span class="math inline">\((g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z})\left\lfloor f \right\rceil = g \, \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil + \mathcal{Z}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\((g \, df + dh)\left\lceil \mathcal{X} \right\rfloor = g \, df\left\lceil \mathcal{X} \right\rfloor + dh\left\lceil \mathcal{X} \right\rfloor\)</span>.</p></li>
<li class="dg-labelled"><span class="dg-item-label">(c)</span> <p>A vector field acts <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}\)</span>-linearly on scalar fields and satisfies the Leibniz rule, <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g f \right\rceil = \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil f + g \, \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil\)</span>.</p></li>
<li class="dg-labelled"><span class="dg-item-label">(d)</span> <p>The connection satisfies property 4, <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{g\mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}} \mathcal{Y} = g \, \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} + \nabla_\mathcal{Z} \mathcal{Y}\)</span>, property 2, and the product rule <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_\mathcal{Y}(g \, \mathcal{X}) = \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X} + g \, \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X}\)</span>.</p></li>
</ol>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p><strong>First entry:</strong>  The vector field <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y})\)</span> does not depend on the covector field, so linearity in the first entry is just property (b) of the module <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma T^*\mathcal{M}\)</span>:  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \mathtt{T}(g \, df + dh, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y})
            &amp;= (g \, df + dh)\left\lceil \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \right\rfloor
            = g \, df\left\lceil \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \right\rfloor + dh\left\lceil \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \right\rfloor \\
            &amp;= g \, \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) + \mathtt{T}(dh, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}).
        \end{align*}</span></p></li>
<li><p><strong>Second entry, the commutator:</strong>  The only term requiring some work is the commutator. Letting <span class="math inline">\([g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}]\)</span> act on an arbitrary <span class="math inline">\(f \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>, and using (b) and then (c):  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            [g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}]\left\lfloor f \right\rceil
            &amp;= (g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z})\left\lfloor \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil
            - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor (g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z})\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil \\
            &amp;= g \, \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil + \mathcal{Z}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil
            - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \, \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Z}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil \\
            &amp;= g \, \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil + \mathcal{Z}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil
            - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil - g \, \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil
            - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Z}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil \\
            &amp;= g \, [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}]\left\lfloor f \right\rceil + [\mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}]\left\lfloor f \right\rceil
            - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil.
        \end{align*}</span>  Since this holds for every <span class="math inline">\(f\)</span>, and using (b) once more,  <span class="math display">\[
            [g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}] = g \, [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}] + [\mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}] - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X}.
        \]</span>  The commutator is therefore <em>not</em> <span class="math inline">\(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>-linear: the last term, involving a derivative of <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span>, spoils it.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Second entry, the remaining terms:</strong>  By (d), the first two terms of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{V}\)</span> give  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \nabla_{g\mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}} \mathcal{Y}    &amp;= g \, \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} + \nabla_\mathcal{Z} \mathcal{Y}, \\
            \nabla_\mathcal{Y}(g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}) &amp;= \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X} + g \, \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X} + \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{Z},
        \end{align*}</span>  so that the second one also produces a non-tensorial term, <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X}\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Second entry, collecting terms:</strong>  Putting the three contributions together,  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \mathcal{V}(g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y})
            &amp;= g \, \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} + \nabla_\mathcal{Z} \mathcal{Y}
            - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X} - g \, \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{Z}
            - g \, [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}] - [\mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}] + \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X} \\
            &amp;= g \, \big( \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X} - [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}] \big)
            + \big( \nabla_\mathcal{Z} \mathcal{Y} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{Z} - [\mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}] \big)
            = g \, \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) + \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}),
        \end{align*}</span>  where the two non-tensorial terms <span class="math inline">\(\mp \, \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X}\)</span>, one coming from the product rule and the other from the commutator, cancel exactly. Finally, by (a),  <span class="math display">\[
            \mathtt{T}(df, g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y})
            = df\left\lceil g \, \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) + \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}) \right\rfloor
            = g \, \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) + \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}).
        \]</span></p></li>
</ul>
<p>Linearity in the third entry needs no separate proof: since <span class="math inline">\([\mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{X}] = -[\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}]\)</span>, the torsion is antisymmetric in its last two entries, <span class="math inline">\(\mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) = -\mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{X})\)</span>, and linearity in the third entry follows from linearity in the second. Hence <span class="math inline">\(\mathtt{T}\)</span> is a <span class="math inline">\((1,2)\)</span>-tensor field. <span class="dg-hfill"></span><span class="math inline">\(\square\)</span></p>
```
